annotations.title: He added this aboue al.
annotations.text: The fault of Princes and other great men, that can not only not abide to heare their faults, but alſo puniſh by death or impriſonment ſuch as reprehend them for the ſame (ſpecially if they warne them, as Prophets and Prieſts doe, from God) is exceding great.

annotations.title: Of Heli.
annotations.text: ◦ Whereas in S. Matthew, Iacob is father to Ioſeph, and here Heli, the caſe was thus. Mathan (named in S. Matthew) of his wife called Eſcha begat Iacob: and after his death, Melchi (named here in S. Luke) of the ſame woman begat Heli: ſo that Iacob and Heli were brethren of one mother. This Heli therfore marrying and dying without iſſue: Iacob his brother, according to the Law married his wife, and begat Ioſeph, and ſo raiſed vp ſeede to his brother Heli. Whereby it came to paſſe, that Iacob vvas the natural father of Ioſeph, which as (S. Matthew ſaith) begat him: and Heli vvas his legal father according to the Law, as S. Luke ſignifieth. Euſeb. li. 1 Ec. Hiſt. c. 7 Hiero. in c. 1 Mat. Aug. li. 2 c. 2. 3 de cons. Euang.

notes.text: The reconciliation of Matthew and Luke in our Sauiours petigree.
